primary_sources.used_for: US bunk-bed scope, accepted third-party testing and children product certification; coordinated guard/mattress/opening review. No universal fabrication dimensions supplied.

US reference and scope; required under-six upper-bunk warning in section 1513.6. Age six or more does not establish suitability. Elevated-bed classification is not excluded merely because there is no lower bed.
Furniture/TV restraint according to manufacturer instructions and avoiding tempting items high on furniture. Product/substrate-specific installation remains required.

Falling-lid and automatic-latch entrapment hazard identification. Historical warning is not presented as a current standard edition; no claim that soft-close, natural material or open storage automatically proves safety.

content_review.M11: Complete cable route and connector access, device-specific ventilation, withdrawal/service and reflection; project changes propagated to sections/services/parts and referenced handover criteria. No guessed vent or anchor specifications.
content_review.M12: Complete bed envelope rather than mattress alone; exercise 3200−1800−400−400=600 total, split 300 per side, explicitly not access approval; mattress/frame/support compatibility and load path do not prove capacity; appearance, attachment and removable cover separated; coordinated finishes do not prove interchangeable drawers.
content_review.M13: School-age use is distinct from infant/toddler needs. No age-only dimensions or load claims. Pull-out states include motion hazards and complete system compatibility; no child hazard trial. Raised-bed figures are hazard maps, not construction plans. Four-year-old upper-bunk proposal rejected, verified alternative still required. Product identity, market, testing/certification and assembly instructions required before acceptance. Desk fit, furniture restraint and lid/material risks are reviewed separately.
